title: Control Charts: inspect a campaign with explicit controls and limits
description: Open the specialist tool inside QC, load a clearly synthetic thirty-plate campaign, check the selected control and baseline, and export independently verified chart points.
objectives: Find Control Charts inside QC and load the supplied synthetic CSV.
Distinguish well-level input rows from plate-level means and select exactly one control.
Compare rule sets, change and restore the control and baseline, and read the resulting warnings.
Export the actual points table without claiming an image export or biological validation.
prerequisite: The CSV at tools/tutorials/fixtures/control_chart_campaign.csv is entirely synthetic, adapted from the application's seeded test campaign: thirty fictitious plates, three wells per control type per plate, and a programmed upward drift after plate twenty. The dates are illustrative order labels, not acquisition records. This specialist panel currently has no Load test data button; no microscopy download, model, GPU analysis or AI request is used. The old two-plate recording was rejected because the application refused to estimate limits. The current narrow settings column clips long choices when closed; the real open dropdowns expose their full names. The optional Z-prime and re-estimation modes are not exercised here.

scenes.narration: Open QC, then its Control Charts button. This specialist workflow charts repeated controls across a campaign. Our supplied CSV is explicitly synthetic, including the drift: it demonstrates the software, not an acquired experiment or a validated assay.

Choose Load table and open the example CSV. It contains two hundred and seventy well-level rows: thirty plates, each with three negative-control, three positive-control and three sample wells. The chart will show one selected-control mean per plate, not one point per cell.

Check Plate, Run order, Measurement and Control column against the displayed names. Select only neg in Control is. This list allows multiple selections; leaving every level unselected charts all rows, so never assume that loading the file has already selected your intended control.

Open Sigma from to read its full choices. Auto chooses the subgroup estimator here because each plate has three selected wells. The limits use baseline within-plate variation, adjusted for the mean's sample size, rather than the standard deviation of the whole drifting series.

Rules offers the usual four, all eight, or Limits only. More rules also create more opportunities for false alarms. We choose Limits only to isolate the three-sigma rule; changing this dropdown recomputes the chart without a separate Run button.

Baseline plates is twenty: P zero one through P twenty set the limits, which are applied to the remaining plates. Nine points, P twenty-two through P thirty, exceed the upper limit. The report and rule table identify them; these programmed signals are not biological discoveries.

Untick neg and select only pos. The chart now shows the other control's means and its own baseline limits, with no rule-one violations in this example. A quiet chart alone does not prove an assay is valid. Restore neg before continuing.

Change Baseline plates to twelve and watch the centre and limits change, then restore twenty. The app requires at least eight baseline plates, but that minimum is not a recommendation. Plan and justify the baseline; do not tune it simply to remove unwanted alerts.

With the original control and twenty-plate baseline restored, choose Export points and save a separate CSV. It contains thirty rows with plate identity, order, mean, subgroup size and spread, limits, standardized distance, baseline membership and fired rules. This is not a chart-image or full-configuration export.

Every exported identity and numeric field was checked against the source CSV, including rule-one flags. The original input is unchanged. For scripted use, the control chart widget module exposes ControlChartSpec and control_chart; its result provides points_frame. Keep your input, settings and acquisition notes together when investigating real alerts.
